Review
sections.text: Jinhsi is a 5-star Spectro Broadblade main damage dealer who is well-known for her lightning-fast rotations, and being the strongest 1.x DPS on her release. She defined the entire early meta of Wuthering Waves, via her accessibility in teammates and her ease of use, with plenty of room for optimization in very unique ways. Her playstyle, which places a particular emphasis on Animation and Swap Cancelling, alongside mid-air combat and damage concentrated in huge AoE nukes, has gotten many (including the writer of this review) smitten with the way that she flips Wuthering Waves gameplay on its head.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
sections.text:
Jinhsi’s Forte mechanics are the focus of her kit by a long shot - almost all of her kit’s most essential features are concentrated there.
 First of all, her Forte gauge. This is used to empower her special Skill, the biggest nuke she can unleash on enemies. Incandescence stacks up to 50, and any time any character inflicts damage of a given attribute, she gains 1 stack, once per 3 seconds. 2 stacks are applied on a separate timer per Coordinated Attack of a given element. This means one element can trigger each effect on a 3s cooldown depending on the type of attack. After having cast Jinhsi’s Outro however, the cooldown of each lowers from 3s to 1s for 20s.
 The nuke Skill that is empowered by her Forte gauge is called Illuminous Epiphany. Jinhsi can activate this after the fourth stage of her empowered mid-air attacks. This Skill has a solid base multiplier that gets increased by massive amounts depending on her Incandescence stacks. At full power, this is still one of the hardest-hitting attacks in the entire game. Every 25s, Jinhsi gets a free Outro that does not consume any Concerto Energy after casting this Skill.
 Jinhsi enters this empowered mid-air state, called Incarnation, via a special Skill called Overflowing Radiance, that she can activate either via her Intro (instantly) or after casting the fourth stage of her regular Basic Attack chain (which takes time). She gains an entirely new set of attacks that she may cast until she reaches her empowered Skill, at which point the state ends and she may switch out until her next damage window.

sections.heading: Rotation Concepts
sections.text:
The way Jinhsi rotates can be extremely varied depending on the team composition. She has many ways to access her key attacks, and can choose to frontload or backload her damage depending on the situation. Her damage is mostly concentrated within her empowered Skill and Ultimate, so she will rotate around those two abilities. This also gives her an increased affinity for crit-fishing - that is to say, if her 2 key abilities crit, but others do not, then that’s still okay, so making builds with lower CRIT Rate, higher CRIT DMG, and resetting runs until her key abilities do crit is totally possible and leads to optimized Jinhsi scores.
 First of all, the fact that she gains an Outro for free every 25s is for a very good reason: It is intended for her to rotate by doing 2 Skills per loop, so while your Support will rotate once, your Hybrid and Jinhsi herself will rotate twice per full team loop. This works out if and only if you plan your rotations correctly.
 Since Jinhsi can rotate extremely quickly, maintaining your entire team’s array of buffs by ensuring the rotation is under 30s is thankfully more than doable. The idea is that if Jinhsi has room to kill time, she can cast her mid-air Skill (the unempowered one) for extra damage alongside her usual mid-air Basic Attacks, then she may do so. However, cancelling the Skill that allows her to access this state in the first place via either a Dash or an Ultimate is key to ensuring her rotations stay within appropriate speed, provided your Forte Stack generation is fast.
 Indeed, one of Jinhsi’s main things keeping her from rotating too fast is a need to build up sufficient Forte stacks to power up her nuke to a desirable degree so that she doesn’t overcap on the following rotation (as this would lower her damage significantly). As long as that condition is satisfied, then Jinhsi is free to rotate as fast as she wants, but nonetheless, it’s very important to keep in mind that managing your Forte stacks is key to optimizing.
 Overall, since Jinhsi’s Intro allows her to instantly access her Incarnation state, in Hypercarry team rotations (with 2 Coordinated Attackers like Zhezhi and Verina) it will be standard to make use of it. However, since Jinhsi’s Outro can be cast for free immediately on a 25s cooldown, she must also be the first character to rotate in the team (the idea is to skip as much of her low-damaging attacks as you can to access her Outro immediately before setting up your incoming rotation with your other characters to empower her Skills as quickly as possible). Additionally, in Quickswap, Jinhsi’s Basic chain will be key to enter Incarnation state in some team rotations.
 All of this to say: rotating with Jinhsi is not linear, and her rotations don’t just boil down to “do 4 mid-air attacks, use her empowered skill and swap off”. Jinhsi is way more complicated to optimize than that, love it or hate it. Our Gameplay section should supplement this overview of her rotation concepts quite well to give you an idea of how Jinhsi should rotate most of the time. It’s also worth keeping in mind that her rotations being this potentially optimizable also means her ceiling is much higher than what most people give her credit for.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
sections.text:
Jinhsi is a character who functions extremely uniquely compared to other characters in the game, and this gives her a damage ceiling that’s much higher than what most inexperienced Jinhsi players could imagine about her. Her complexity and uniqueness in her rotation define a distinctly varied character packed with ways to optimize and mix up the way that she is played. Additionally, while her teammate choices are fairly limited for casual players, since Coordinated Attackers tend to be a necessity for the easy Hypercarry compositions to function, this does not mean Jinhsi is struggling to find teammates for Quickswap compositions or that she lacks variety in gameplay even for Hypercarry playstyles.
 She has easily accessible teammates in the form of Yuanwu and Verina (or Shorekeeper), who make for a basic Jinhsi Hypercarry team that can evolve into Quickswap with the addition of Changli as a second teammate for example, or even Zhezhi, Yinlin and Cantarella to vary Hypercarry team choices. However,Cantarella is fairly anti-synergistic with Jinhsi due to being locked by her long 25s Ultimate and Forte Skill cooldowns to have smooth rotations, so Zhezhi (and to a lesser degree Yinlin) remain her primary teammate choices (Yinlin being more quickswap-friendly but less accessible than Zhezhi despite having similar if not slightly worse results when fully optimized for both).
 In conclusion, Jinhsi is one of the most original characters ever created in Wuthering Waves. She may struggle in Whimpering Wastes by design since all of her damage is concentrated in a few nukes that she tends to overkill enemies with, and she may struggle nowadays in Tower of Adversity due to a lack of new optimal teammates since v1.2-1.3, but this doesn’t change that she has room to persist in content like Endstate Matrix due to her highly optimizable ceiling and room for crit-fishing. While she is nowadays powercrept, and it’s difficult to argue pulling for her, she may be serviceable in Tower/Matrix for those who are still willing to give her a chance!

sections.heading: Rotation & Gameplay
sections.text: Jinhsi is one of the most complex and optimizable characters in Wuthering Waves. She is able to cancel a ton of animations and play in quickswap in a much more difficult manner than an overwhelming majority of the character cast. This section will go in full detail on how to exploit all of Jinhsi’s numerous rotation techniques, but we will also make sure to provide an easy-to-follow rotation which can be used in her standard teams to a very efficient degree.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
sections.text:
Something to note before going into Jinhsi’s rotations is that she has very unique mechanics in her kit that allow her to get several Outros and Forte Skill nukes per rotation. Via her Unison mechanic, using her Forte Skill (accessed after doing her 4th Basic Attack in Incarnation state, itself accessed via her 2nd Resonance Skill) instantly gives her an Outro every 25s, no Concerto buildup required. However, she also retains access to her Concerto Energy gauge which can also allow her to get an Outro. Additionally, the aforementioned Forte Skill is empowered by the amount of Incandescence stacks she’s built, up to 50 stacks, its generation being accelerated by her Outro.
 As a result, when keeping all of those factors in mind, Jinhsi will ideally want to act as the first character to get her Outro in an ideal rotation, executing a quick, low-power Forte Skill to empower the next one by a significant amount once the rest of the team has applied their buffs onto her. Generally speaking, every 2 Forte Skills alongside one Ultimate, Jinhsi will get access to her standard Outro, while the Unison effect will be activated every other Forte Skill.
 This lets Jinhsi get 2 Outros per rotation cycle — and it doesn’t prevent your secondary buffer from Introing into Jinhsi twice, either. Jinhsi is indeed a character that rotates differently from the strict majority of the character cast; she wants to build 2 Intros and 2 Outros per rotation cycle, getting a total of 2 Forte Skill nukes as well as 1 Ultimate before you go back to rotating into your general Support (typically Shorekeeper or Verina). The timings on upkeeping every buff for both of her Forte skill nukes is undeniably tight, however it’s the core element of what allows Jinhsi to perform at a level close to the current top tiers.
 💡 Tip

sections.heading: Echo Timing
sections.text: For all of her rotations, Jinhsi’s Echo Timing is very free-flow since she runs a Summon in the form of Jué which doesn’t have any specific activation conditions. When using the optimized Jump Cancel opener, it should be utilized as a means to generate an air current to quickly cancel all of her Basic Attacks and access her Forte Skill. Outside of that, she’s free to use it at any point in her rotation (the most recommended would be right before a Forte Skill nuke to try and catch the 2 of them per rotation cycle).

 Jinhsi can also cancel any of her attacks via a Dash and her base Incarnation Skill (Crescent Divinity).

 Jinhsi can cancel her Basic P4 instantly via her Overflowing Radiance skill in order to enter Incarnation quicker, which makes it do 0 damage. The same can be done for her Incarnation Basic P4 with Illuminous Epiphany, however the full damage is retained in this scenario.

sections.heading: Expert Optimizations (Swap & Jump Cancels)
sections.text:
Alongside the optimization knowledge detailed above, a few more details can be kept in mind in order to really take Jinhsi to a completely different ceiling than what she previously could achieve at a baseline:
 Once Jinhsi’s Incarnation state ends, it’s possible to input a Mid-Air Attack before swapping in order to squeeze slightly more damage at no rotation time cost.

 Jinhsi additionally has access to several Jump Cancel opportunities during her Opener rotation. This is because her Echo, Jué, generates an updraft when it is casted, which can be used to activate your Glider at very low heights. If done quickly and assuming Jinhsi is on the ground when initiating her first Incarnation Basic Attack (and the beginning of the second), this can allow Jinhsi to get her Illuminous Epiphany skill nearly instantly in the Opener (just a couple of seconds are needed!), accelerating her setup to being lightning-fast. Note that this is Jinhsi’s most difficult technique to learn since it requires precise positioning and fast inputs, hence why it’s only used in the Opener (even though it could theoretically be used to cancel one of her Basics at lightspeed in every rotation, it’s simply unrealistic to do so and generally not worth it for DPS unless trying to finish a boss with her Forte Skill’s damage — but she has more realistic ways to do so quickly).

 If needed in order to quickly finish a boss, Jinhsi can entirely forget about her Crescent Divinity skill and Dash Cancel her Incarnation Basics P2 and P3 instead similarly to her Opener, in order to access her Forte Skill as quickly as possible.

 Finally, the knowledge below applies to Jinhsi teams that don’t give her desirable Outro buffs:
 Jinhsi can operate without Intros entirely and build up her Forte Skills before she even gets a single Intro from any other character. sections.heading: Rotation Concepts
sections.text:
The way Jinhsi rotates can be extremely varied depending on the team composition. She has many ways to access her key attacks, and can choose to frontload or backload her damage depending on the situation. Her damage is mostly concentrated within her empowered Skill and Ultimate, so she will rotate around those two abilities. This also gives her an increased affinity for crit-fishing - that is to say, if her 2 key abilities crit, but others do not, then that’s still okay, so making builds with lower CRIT Rate, higher CRIT DMG, and resetting runs until her key abilities do crit is totally possible and leads to optimized Jinhsi scores.
 First of all, the fact that she gains an Outro for free every 25s is for a very good reason: It is intended for her to rotate by doing 2 Skills per loop, so while your Support will rotate once, your Hybrid and Jinhsi herself will rotate twice per full team loop. This works out if and only if you plan your rotations correctly.
 Since Jinhsi can rotate extremely quickly, maintaining your entire team’s array of buffs by ensuring the rotation is under 30s is thankfully more than doable. The idea is that if Jinhsi has room to kill time, she can cast her mid-air Skill (the unempowered one) for extra damage alongside her usual mid-air Basic Attacks, then she may do so. However, cancelling the Skill that allows her to access this state in the first place via either a Dash or an Ultimate is key to ensuring her rotations stay within appropriate speed, provided your Forte Stack generation is fast.
 Indeed, one of Jinhsi’s main things keeping her from rotating too fast is a need to build up sufficient Forte stacks to power up her nuke to a desirable degree so that she doesn’t overcap on the following rotation (as this would lower her damage significantly). As long as that condition is satisfied, then Jinhsi is free to rotate as fast as she wants, but nonetheless, it’s very important to keep in mind that managing your Forte stacks is key to optimizing.
 Overall, since Jinhsi’s Intro allows her to instantly access her Incarnation state, in Hypercarry team rotations (with 2 Coordinated Attackers like Zhezhi and Verina) it will be standard to make use of it. However, since Jinhsi’s Outro can be cast for free immediately on a 25s cooldown, she must also be the first character to rotate in the team (the idea is to skip as much of her low-damaging attacks as you can to access her Outro immediately before setting up your incoming rotation with your other characters to empower her Skills as quickly as possible). Additionally, in Quickswap, Jinhsi’s Basic chain will be key to enter Incarnation state in some team rotations.
 All of this to say: rotating with Jinhsi is not linear, and her rotations don’t just boil down to “do 4 mid-air attacks, use her empowered skill and swap off”. Jinhsi is way more complicated to optimize than that, love it or hate it. Our Gameplay section should supplement this overview of her rotation concepts quite well to give you an idea of how Jinhsi should rotate most of the time. It’s also worth keeping in mind that her rotations being this potentially optimizable also means her ceiling is much higher than what most people give her credit for.

 Review
 Jinhsi is a 5-star Spectro Broadblade main damage dealer who is well-known for her lightning-fast rotations, and being the strongest 1.x DPS on her release. She defined the entire early meta of Wuthering Waves, via her accessibility in teammates and her ease of use, with plenty of room for optimization in very unique ways. Her playstyle, which places a particular emphasis on Animation and Swap Cancelling, alongside mid-air combat and damage concentrated in huge AoE nukes, has gotten many (including the writer of this review) smitten with the way that she flips Wuthering Waves gameplay on its head.
 Key Mechanics
 Jinhsi’s Forte mechanics are the focus of her kit by a long shot - almost all of her kit’s most essential features are concentrated there.
 First of all, her Forte gauge. This is used to empower her special Skill, the biggest nuke she can unleash on enemies. Incandescence stacks up to 50, and any time any character inflicts damage of a given attribute, she gains 1 stack, once per 3 seconds. 2 stacks are applied on a separate timer per Coordinated Attack of a given element. This means one element can trigger each effect on a 3s cooldown depending on the type of attack. After having cast Jinhsi’s Outro however, the cooldown of each lowers from 3s to 1s for 20s.
 The nuke Skill that is empowered by her Forte gauge is called Illuminous Epiphany. Jinhsi can activate this after the fourth stage of her empowered mid-air attacks. This Skill has a solid base multiplier that gets increased by massive amounts depending on her Incandescence stacks. At full power, this is still one of the hardest-hitting attacks in the entire game. Every 25s, Jinhsi gets a free Outro that does not consume any Concerto Energy after casting this Skill.
 Jinhsi enters this empowered mid-air state, called Incarnation, via a special Skill called Overflowing Radiance, that she can activate either via her Intro (instantly) or after casting the fourth stage of her regular Basic Attack chain (which takes time). She gains an entirely new set of attacks that she may cast until she reaches her empowered Skill, at which point the state ends and she may switch out until her next damage window.
 Rotation Concepts
 The way Jinhsi rotates can be extremely varied depending on the team composition. She has many ways to access her key attacks, and can choose to frontload or backload her damage depending on the situation. Her damage is mostly concentrated within her empowered Skill and Ultimate, so she will rotate around those two abilities. This also gives her an increased affinity for crit-fishing - that is to say, if her 2 key abilities crit, but others do not, then that’s still okay, so making builds with lower CRIT Rate, higher CRIT DMG, and resetting runs until her key abilities do crit is totally possible and leads to optimized Jinhsi scores.
 First of all, the fact that she gains an Outro for free every 25s is for a very good reason: It is intended for her to rotate by doing 2 Skills per loop, so while your Support will rotate once, your Hybrid and Jinhsi herself will rotate twice per full team loop. This works out if and only if you plan your rotations correctly.
 Since Jinhsi can rotate extremely quickly, maintaining your entire team’s array of buffs by ensuring the rotation is under 30s is thankfully more than doable. The idea is that if Jinhsi has room to kill time, she can cast her mid-air Skill (the unempowered one) for extra damage alongside her usual mid-air Basic Attacks, then she may do so. However, cancelling the Skill that allows her to access this state in the first place via either a Dash or an Ultimate is key to ensuring her rotations stay within appropriate speed, provided your Forte Stack generation is fast.
 Indeed, one of Jinhsi’s main things keeping her from rotating too fast is a need to build up sufficient Forte stacks to power up her nuke to a desirable degree so that she doesn’t overcap on the following rotation (as this would lower her damage significantly). As long as that condition is satisfied, then Jinhsi is free to rotate as fast as she wants, but nonetheless, it’s very important to keep in mind that managing your Forte stacks is key to optimizing.
 Overall, since Jinhsi’s Intro allows her to instantly access her Incarnation state, in Hypercarry team rotations (with 2 Coordinated Attackers like Zhezhi and Verina) it will be standard to make use of it. However, since Jinhsi’s Outro can be cast for free immediately on a 25s cooldown, she must also be the first character to rotate in the team (the idea is to skip as much of her low-damaging attacks as you can to access her Outro immediately before setting up your incoming rotation with your other characters to empower her Skills as quickly as possible). Additionally, in Quickswap, Jinhsi’s Basic chain will be key to enter Incarnation state in some team rotations.
 All of this to say: rotating with Jinhsi is not linear, and her rotations don’t just boil down to “do 4 mid-air attacks, use her empowered skill and swap off”. Jinhsi is way more complicated to optimize than that, love it or hate it. Our Gameplay section should supplement this overview of her rotation concepts quite well to give you an idea of how Jinhsi should rotate most of the time. It’s also worth keeping in mind that her rotations being this potentially optimizable also means her ceiling is much higher than what most people give her credit for.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 Jinhsi is a character who functions extremely uniquely compared to other characters in the game, and this gives her a damage ceiling that’s much higher than what most inexperienced Jinhsi players could imagine about her. Her complexity and uniqueness in her rotation define a distinctly varied character packed with ways to optimize and mix up the way that she is played. Additionally, while her teammate choices are fairly limited for casual players, since Coordinated Attackers tend to be a necessity for the easy Hypercarry compositions to function, this does not mean Jinhsi is struggling to find teammates for Quickswap compositions or that she lacks variety in gameplay even for Hypercarry playstyles.
 She has easily accessible teammates in the form of Yuanwu and Verina (or Shorekeeper), who make for a basic Jinhsi Hypercarry team that can evolve into Quickswap with the addition of Changli as a second teammate for example, or even Zhezhi, Yinlin and Cantarella to vary Hypercarry team choices. However,Cantarella is fairly anti-synergistic with Jinhsi due to being locked by her long 25s Ultimate and Forte Skill cooldowns to have smooth rotations, so Zhezhi (and to a lesser degree Yinlin) remain her primary teammate choices (Yinlin being more quickswap-friendly but less accessible than Zhezhi despite having similar if not slightly worse results when fully optimized for both).
 In conclusion, Jinhsi is one of the most original characters ever created in Wuthering Waves. She may struggle in Whimpering Wastes by design since all of her damage is concentrated in a few nukes that she tends to overkill enemies with, and she may struggle nowadays in Tower of Adversity due to a lack of new optimal teammates since v1.2-1.3, but this doesn’t change that she has room to persist in content like Endstate Matrix due to her highly optimizable ceiling and room for crit-fishing. While she is nowadays powercrept, and it’s difficult to argue pulling for her, she may be serviceable in Tower/Matrix for those who are still willing to give her a chance!

 Jinhsi is one of the most complex and optimizable characters in Wuthering Waves. She is able to cancel a ton of animations and play in quickswap in a much more difficult manner than an overwhelming majority of the character cast. This section will go in full detail on how to exploit all of Jinhsi’s numerous rotation techniques, but we will also make sure to provide an easy-to-follow rotation which can be used in her standard teams to a very efficient degree.
 Key Mechanics
 Something to note before going into Jinhsi’s rotations is that she has very unique mechanics in her kit that allow her to get several Outros and Forte Skill nukes per rotation. Via her Unison mechanic, using her Forte Skill (accessed after doing her 4th Basic Attack in Incarnation state, itself accessed via her 2nd Resonance Skill) instantly gives her an Outro every 25s, no Concerto buildup required. However, she also retains access to her Concerto Energy gauge which can also allow her to get an Outro. Additionally, the aforementioned Forte Skill is empowered by the amount of Incandescence stacks she’s built, up to 50 stacks, its generation being accelerated by her Outro.
 As a result, when keeping all of those factors in mind, Jinhsi will ideally want to act as the first character to get her Outro in an ideal rotation, executing a quick, low-power Forte Skill to empower the next one by a significant amount once the rest of the team has applied their buffs onto her. Generally speaking, every 2 Forte Skills alongside one Ultimate, Jinhsi will get access to her standard Outro, while the Unison effect will be activated every other Forte Skill.
 This lets Jinhsi get 2 Outros per rotation cycle — and it doesn’t prevent your secondary buffer from Introing into Jinhsi twice, either. Jinhsi is indeed a character that rotates differently from the strict majority of the character cast; she wants to build 2 Intros and 2 Outros per rotation cycle, getting a total of 2 Forte Skill nukes as well as 1 Ultimate before you go back to rotating into your general Support (typically Shorekeeper or Verina). The timings on upkeeping every buff for both of her Forte skill nukes is undeniably tight, however it’s the core element of what allows Jinhsi to perform at a level close to the current top tiers.

In those time windows, it’s possible to switch out of Jinhsi into any other character to weave in a few attacks before switching back into her, at little to no rotation time cost.
